In a longitudinal wave, the distance between two neighbouring compressions (or two neighbouring rarefactions) is one wavelength.
Subsonic (infrasonic) sound has a frequency below 20 Hz, too low for humans to hear. Above 20,000 Hz is ultrasonic.

A barometer measures atmospheric pressure. An altimeter measures height, a fathometer measures sea depth and an ammeter measures current.
In Newton's third law, action and reaction are equal and opposite, and they always act on two different objects. That is why they do not cancel each other.
In myopia (short sight) the image forms in front of the retina. A concave lens spreads the light a little so the image falls on the retina.
Pure (distilled) water has almost no dissolved salts, so it conducts electricity very poorly. It is a bad conductor.

As the body falls in vacuum, potential energy turns into kinetic energy, and with no air resistance nothing is lost. So the total mechanical energy stays the same. Its speed and momentum keep increasing.
The magnitude of an earthquake is measured on the Richter scale. "Righter" is a wrong spelling.

value: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed
reasoning: By the law of conservation of energy, energy can neither be created nor destroyed. It only changes from one form to another.
Polyester (such as PET) is used to make cloth and also strong, unbreakable bottles and jars.
Hydrogen has the highest calorific value of all fuels, about 150,000 kJ/kg, far more than LPG, CNG or biogas.
Phosphorus catches fire in air, so it is kept under water. Sodium reacts strongly with water and air, so it is kept in kerosene.
When coal is heated strongly without air, the black porous solid left behind is coke. Coal tar is a thick liquid by-product.

Melamine resists fire and heat, so fire fighters' uniforms are coated with it.

Iron is more reactive than copper, so it pushes copper out of copper sulphate solution. Platinum, gold and silver are less reactive than copper.

Meteors are small bodies that burn up as they enter Earth's atmosphere, leaving a bright streak. They are called shooting stars.

The thyroid gland needs iodine to make thyroxine. Too little iodine causes goitre.
Plant cells, as in the mango tree and cactus, have cell walls of cellulose. The bacterial cell wall is made of a different substance (peptidoglycan).
Scattering seeds by hand over the field is called broadcasting. A seed drill sows them with a tool.
Plastids are the coloured bodies in the cytoplasm of plant cells. The green ones, with chlorophyll, are chloroplasts.
The pancreas makes insulin, which controls the level of sugar (glucose) in the blood.
Leaving a field uncultivated for one or more seasons so the soil can recover is called fallowing.
In the nitrogen cycle, Nitrobacter bacteria change nitrites into nitrates, which plants can take up.
Yeast is a fungus made of a single cell, and its cell has a proper nucleus. So it is both unicellular and a eukaryote.
Citrus canker is caused by bacteria. Rust and smut are fungal diseases, and mosaic disease is caused by a virus.

Bandipur in Karnataka is a National Park (and a tiger reserve).

A mature plant cell has one large central vacuole that fills most of the cell.

The egg released from the ovary meets the sperm in the fallopian tube (oviduct), where fertilisation happens.

After the infection, the body keeps antibodies and memory against smallpox, so it fights the germ quickly if it comes again.
